topics.topic: Handling of bounded multipart-head parsing and whether failures affect the session idle period
questions: What happens when the multipart head exceeds the bound, is truncated, is malformed, has no file part, or fails while being read, and does that request reach the session check and restart the idle period?

What happens when the multipart head is malformed, truncated, ends before the file part, or exceeds `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`, and does that request count as having arrived for session validity and idle restart?

What happens when the multipart head is malformed, truncated, exceeds the bound, cannot be read, lacks the file-part headers, or ends before a file part appears, and does such a request reach the session check and restart the idle limit?

quotes:
The CSRF value the first part carries, the delimiter that ends the file
part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length
less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line
end, or none when the request declared none; or that the head is not of that form — no multipart content type or
boundary, a first part that is not the CSRF field, no second part that is
the file — or is longer than the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`
constant, or declares less than that head and the closing delimiter, or the
request's stream fails or ends while the head is read — with none of these
values.

None: a head of another form answers no CSRF value, and the upload is
refused at stage (1) as a change without one (A04 rule 6, A13 rule 5).

At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: State 5 says every listed malformed, truncated, over-bound or failed head produces no head values, is refused at stage (1), and still restarts the idle period when the request carries a valid session.

topics.topic: When the upload arrival timestamp is captured for session validity
questions: Is the monotonic arrival reading captured immediately when the bounded head finishes, before waiting for the import or session lock, or only when the locked session check runs?
Is the upload’s arrival reading captured at the instant the bounded head finishes, or taken later when `operations` invokes `owner_sessions`?
Is session validity evaluated at the monotonic reading taken immediately when the bounded head finishes, or at a later reading after the request has waited for the import and session locks?

quotes:
Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading` this operation takes when it is called, which for
an upload is after its bounded head has been read (A13 rule 2): a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5). A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2). After the check, a change that touches no uploaded file takes its
place on the session's lock at once; a request that touches one first waits
for the import lock and then takes its place, so the locks are always taken
import first and no place on a session's lock waits for the import lock (A16
rule 2).
judgement.why: State 5 fixes the monotonic reading at the call to admission after the bounded head is read and places all import-lock and session-lock waiting after that check.

topics.topic: Whether request streams follow declared length or actual transport and multipart framing
questions: How can Registry count bytes beyond an understated declared length, or accept a body with no declared length, if the supplied stream ends at the declared length?

For an upload with an absent or understated declared length, does the request-body stream continue to the transport or multipart boundary so Registry can count every received file byte, or does it end at the declared length?
Is the request's declared length authoritative for the stream boundary, or must the stream follow the actual multipart framing and received bytes when the length is absent or false?

quotes:
An import file of exactly 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes, sent by the upload form
with its CSRF field first, is read; one of a byte more is refused, with
no mapping shown, also when its declared length is smaller or absent, and
the file the session kept before stays kept.
judgement.divergence: For an over-limit file with an understated declared length, A19 requires Registry to observe the extra byte and return the over-limit refusal, while the lifecycle passage ends the supplied stream at the understated length so the import reader cannot observe that byte; the owner notices the required size refusal versus a truncated-body result.
judgement.why: The required understated-length size test cannot be satisfied by a request-body stream that ends at the understated declared length.

declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the
limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever
length was declared or whether one was.

topics.topic: Ownership and timing of multipart parsing and file-part stream creation
questions: For an upload, does `owner_interface` read the whole form before calling `operations`, or read only the bounded head and pass the file part unread?
Which named capability produces the file-part stream that ends at the multipart boundary and derives its declared length, and which operation calls it before `migration_import` reads the file?

quotes:
`module:upload_framing`. Read an upload's multipart head alone, so that its
CSRF value travels in the form and the file reaches `migration_import`
unread (A13 rules 5, 7; owner, 2026-11-17).

The CSRF value the first part carries, the delimiter that ends the file
part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length
less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line
end, or none when the request declared none; or that the head is not of that form — no multipart content type or
boundary, a first part that is not the CSRF field, no second part that is
the file — or is longer than the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`
constant, or declares less than that head and the closing delimiter, or the
request's stream fails or ends while the head is read — with none of these
values. The file part's stream is a `MultipartFileBody`, the class
`upload_framing` owns that implements `UploadBody` (State 6); it fails
when the request's stream ends before the closing delimiter, which
`migration_import.read_import_mapping` refuses as `file_unreadable`, as any
stream that fails.

`upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads
the body's head alone and answers the CSRF value and the file part's
declared length; `owner_interface` hands that length and the file part, as
an unread stream that ends where the part ends, to
`operations.perform_owner_operation`, without reading or buffering it.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns bounded parsing and `MultipartFileBody` creation to `upload_framing.read_upload_head`, called by `owner_interface`, which passes the unread file stream through `operations.perform_owner_operation` to the import operation.
